headline: DAR Says ₱57.76 Billion in Agrarian Reform Debt Condoned Under RA 11953
seoTitle: DAR: ₱57.76B Agrarian Reform Debt Condoned | FMB News
seoDescription: DAR says ₱57.76 billion in agrarian reform debt has been condoned under RA 11953, covering more than 610,000 agrarian reform beneficiaries nationwide.
deck: The New Agrarian Emancipation Act erases covered principal, amortizations, interest and penalties, while DAR accelerates individual e-title issuance and farmer support programs.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Agrarian Reform said ₱57.76 billion in agrarian reform beneficiaries' land debt has been condoned under Republic Act No. 11953, the New Agrarian Emancipation Act.

DAR said the law covers unpaid principal loans, amortizations, interest and penalties for more than 610,000 agrarian reform beneficiaries nationwide. The department also reported that beneficiaries collectively earned ₱10.6 billion as of July 2026.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: RA 11953 was designed to remove qualifying agrarian debt and strengthen beneficiaries' ownership of awarded land. DAR officials said beneficiaries outside the condonation coverage may be covered by a payment moratorium under applicable rules.

DAR is also accelerating individual electronic land titles. From January through June, it reported issuing 19,967 e-titles covering 19,006 hectares and benefiting 10,522 agrarian reform beneficiaries.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Removing legacy land debt can free household and farm capital for production, while individual titles can improve tenure security. The longer-term effect will depend on access to credit, markets, infrastructure and farm productivity support in addition to debt relief.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: DAR says it is pursuing partnerships with financial and agricultural agencies, expanding farmer organizations' market access and digitizing land and case-management processes. Progress on e-title issuance and the reach of support programs will determine how much of the debt relief translates into durable income gains.
